entries.note: Needs wire-delta-count only for a known textual conflict: adjacent import hunks in packages/agent/src/agent.ts (Dialect import line) and packages/ai/src/providers/factory-droid.ts (factory-droid/gemini import line); resolve on the rebase after D merges. precheck also names code conflicts with open #17885 (factory-droid.ts) and #17861 (factory-droid/gemini.ts); token-count-policy's own conflict with #17747 is C's. Review (one round) done at b9aedbaf95; findings 1-5 fixed with fail-on-revert tests.

entries.title: fix(coding-agent): stop URL reads returning bot block pages as content
fix(natives): pace Wayland multi-clicks so KDE Qt apps see double clicks
fix(browser): exit a process-local headless Chrome when the process that launched it is killed
fix(natives): keep X11 takeover keys running when the core keyboard switches source
fix(natives): release the X11 virtual keyboard's focus before takeover activates its window
fix(natives): refuse X11 background keys to Qt apps instead of reporting them sent
fix(natives): stop takeover keys into iPhone Mirroring and Screen Sharing from leaving Fn held
fix(natives): refuse background drags on Windows Tk windows
fix(natives): refuse Wayland element input before focusing the element
fix(natives): keep X11 background element typing from raising the element's window
fix(natives): load libpipewire at runtime so released addons capture on Wayland

fix(natives): read GTK3 file dialogs as AT-SPI windows

# An identifier that represent common dependencies (unconditional).
_COMMON_CONDITION = ""

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of the requested crates for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
    ]).pop(package_name, {})

    # Combine all conditional packages so we can easily index over a flat list
    # TODO: Perhaps this should actually return select statements and maintain
    # the conditionals of the dependencies
    flat_deps = {}
    for deps_set in dependencies.values():
        for crate_name, crate_label in deps_set.items():
            flat_deps.update({crate_name: crate_label})

    missing_crates = []
    crate_targets = []
    for crate_target in deps:
        if crate_target not in flat_deps:
            missing_crates.append(crate_target)
        else:
            crate_targets.append(flat_deps[crate_target])

    if missing_crates:
        fail("Could not find crates `{}` among dependencies of `{}`. Available dependencies were `{}`".format(
            missing_crates,
            package_name,
            dependencies,
        ))

    return crate_targets

def crate_edition(package_name = None):
    """Finds the Rust edition for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        package_name (str, optional): The package name whose edition should be
            looked up. Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        str: The Rust edition declared by the package's Cargo.toml file.
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    if package_name not in _CRATE_EDITIONS:
        fail("Tried to get crate_edition for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")

    return _CRATE_EDITIONS[package_name]

def all_crate_deps(
        normal = False, 
        normal_dev = False, 
        proc_macro = False, 
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of all requested direct crate dependencies \
    for the package where this macro is called.

    If no parameters are set, all normal dependencies are returned. Setting any one flag will
    otherwise impact the contents of the returned list.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list.
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not dependencies:
        if dependencies == None:
            fail("Tried to get all_crate_deps for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")
        else:
            return []

    crate_deps = list(dependencies.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).values())
    for condition, deps in dependencies.items():
        crate_deps += selects.with_or({
            tuple(_CONDITIONS[condition]): deps.values(),
            "//conditions:default": [],
        })

    return crate_deps

def aliases(
        normal = False,
        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Produces a map of Crate alias names to their original label

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]
        for triple in condition_triples:
            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

docs/tools/browser.md: Automatic Tern and cmux belong to the interactive omp drawn in that terminal. At startup it sets `PI_TERMINAL_OWNER_PID` to its pid, and every command it runs inherits that, so an omp started from those commands (`omp -p` from the bash tool, a script an eval cell runs) sees a pane owned by another process and does not pick Tern or cmux from it; its open without `app` ends at managed Chromium unless a relay or `browser.cdpUrl` it is configured for comes first. `app.tern: true`, `app.target`, `PI_BROWSER_TERN=1` and `PI_BROWSER_CMUX=1` still select them.

The user's own surfaces are the defaults of the session they talk to. A subagent (a `task` child or an eval `agent()`) skips the relay, Tern and cmux for an open without `app`, even with `browser.relay` on or `PI_BROWSER_RELAY=1`/`PI_BROWSER_TERN=1`/`PI_BROWSER_CMUX=1` set, and goes on to `browser.cdpUrl` or managed Chromium. To use the user's Chrome it needs `app.relay: true`; to adopt an existing Chrome tab, pass `app: { relay: true, target: "<CDP target id>" }`. `app.tern: true` explicitly selects Tern, and `app.target` alone opts into adopting a Tern browser block, not a Chrome tab (configured CDP still takes precedence over target-only Tern selection). A `/tan` clone carries its parent's system prompt, which describes the parent's defaults, and keeps them; an advisor shares its owner's browser and defaults. A subagent reopening a relay tab name its parent opened needs `app.relay: true` too; without it the open fails on the browser kind mismatch.
packages/browser-relay/README.md: - **As the default** — `omp config set browser.relay true` makes the relay the default for **every top-level session using this profile, in every project** (project-level settings, `PI_BROWSER_RELAY`, and an explicit `app` choice still take precedence). Any such session's ordinary `browser.open(...)` call will then drive your real browser, including `omp -p` runs and other background sessions you aren't watching; without `app.target` such a call opens its own background tab in your logged-in profile. Subagents skip the default (and `PI_BROWSER_RELAY=1`) and reach the relay only with `app: { relay: true }`.
packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/tools/: - Omit `app` → settings pick the browser: the user's Chrome through the relay when `browser.relay` is on (`PI_BROWSER_RELAY=1` turns it on even with the setting off, `=0` off), else `browser.cdpUrl`, else Tern inside a Tern pane, else cmux, else managed Chromium (installs on first use). Tern and cmux are skipped when another omp session drawn in that terminal started this one (for example `omp -p` from its bash tool). A subagent skips the relay, Tern and cmux: pass `app.relay: true` or `app.tern: true` when the task needs the user's browser or pane.

- `app.tern: false` skips Tern only: with the relay on it still opens the user's Chrome, so pass `app: { tern: false, relay: false }` to skip both (e.g. parallel scraping, where PiPs would pile up over one pane); a configured `browser.cdpUrl` or cmux still comes before managed Chromium. `app.tern: true` requires Tern; `headed` never chooses between Tern and Chromium. When no Tern window can host a PiP, the open falls back to Chromium and says so.
* Chromium. Tern and cmux are automatic only while no other omp owns the terminal,
* and none of the user's own surfaces (relay, Tern, cmux) is automatic for a subagent.

docs/tools/browser.md: On Chromium tabs, the first `observe()` or `ariaSnapshot()` after an input helper or navigation waits for what the actions since the last look started: the main-frame document, fetch and XHR requests begun since the first of them, then 150 ms without DOM changes. The wait is bounded at 3 seconds, or half the call's own budget when that is shorter, and the page is read as it is after that. A look with no action before it does not wait, a request already open before the action is not waited for, and looks issued together share one wait. The first look after `browser.open` or `goto` counts the requests the page load started.

# An identifier that represent common dependencies (unconditional).
_COMMON_CONDITION = ""

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of the requested crates for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
    ]).pop(package_name, {})

    # Combine all conditional packages so we can easily index over a flat list
    # TODO: Perhaps this should actually return select statements and maintain
    # the conditionals of the dependencies
    flat_deps = {}
    for deps_set in dependencies.values():
        for crate_name, crate_label in deps_set.items():
            flat_deps.update({crate_name: crate_label})

    missing_crates = []
    crate_targets = []
    for crate_target in deps:
        if crate_target not in flat_deps:
            missing_crates.append(crate_target)
        else:
            crate_targets.append(flat_deps[crate_target])

    if missing_crates:
        fail("Could not find crates `{}` among dependencies of `{}`. Available dependencies were `{}`".format(
            missing_crates,
            package_name,
            dependencies,
        ))

    return crate_targets

def crate_edition(package_name = None):
    """Finds the Rust edition for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        package_name (str, optional): The package name whose edition should be
            looked up. Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        str: The Rust edition declared by the package's Cargo.toml file.
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    if package_name not in _CRATE_EDITIONS:
        fail("Tried to get crate_edition for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")

    return _CRATE_EDITIONS[package_name]

def all_crate_deps(
        normal = False, 
        normal_dev = False, 
        proc_macro = False, 
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of all requested direct crate dependencies \
    for the package where this macro is called.

    If no parameters are set, all normal dependencies are returned. Setting any one flag will
    otherwise impact the contents of the returned list.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list.
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not dependencies:
        if dependencies == None:
            fail("Tried to get all_crate_deps for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")
        else:
            return []

    crate_deps = list(dependencies.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).values())
    for condition, deps in dependencies.items():
        crate_deps += selects.with_or({
            tuple(_CONDITIONS[condition]): deps.values(),
            "//conditions:default": [],
        })

    return crate_deps

def aliases(
        normal = False,
        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Produces a map of Crate alias names to their original label

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]
        for triple in condition_triples:
            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

docs/computer-use.md: Window input defaults to background routes that do not move the user's pointer or deliberately activate the target. When a call's background route is unavailable, `computer.backgroundFallback` decides what happens. With `takeover` (the default) the tool reruns that one call in takeover, hands focus back to the app the user was in, and adds a line to the run output naming the reason, saying the input was delivered, and saying where focus ended, such as `click ran in takeover because window 42 (Python) uses the Tk toolkit, …; the input was delivered, and focus returned to Notes`. Where focus ended is the front process macOS or Windows reports once the takeover finished; where that is unknown (Linux, or an unreadable front process) the line says focus was not confirmed. On macOS focus returns even if the user kept typing during the takeover (X11 and Windows run the rerun as plain takeover, which yields to user activity); only a third app (neither the user's app nor the target) that became active during the action keeps focus, and the output says so. With `refuse` the call throws `BackgroundUnavailable` with the reason and says the user's setting keeps the agent in the background, so no takeover happened. `refuse` also beats the model: `takeover: true`, `raise()`, an AX `raise` action, `apps.open(…, { activate: true })` or `{ reveal: true }`, `control.acquire` (a grant acquired earlier is released), input to the desktop or a display target and, off macOS, `el.focus()` throw `BackgroundUnavailable` before anything is sent, naming the background route where there is one. Under `takeover`, a call that passes `takeover` itself is never rerun: `takeover: true` takes over at once and restores focus only if the user did not act during it, and `takeover: false` stays background. Takeover temporarily activates the exact target and posts real input, then restores focus and pointer position. OS activation restrictions can still refuse takeover. Desktop-root pointer helpers (`computer.click`, …) always drive the user's real pointer.

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,

    # TODO: Perhaps this should actually return select statements and maintain
    # the conditionals of the dependencies
    flat_deps = {}
    for deps_set in dependencies.values():
        for crate_name, crate_label in deps_set.items():
            flat_deps.update({crate_name: crate_label})

    crate_targets = []
    for crate_target in deps:

    if package_name == None:

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]
        for triple in condition_triples:
            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {

        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.

                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))

    if normal:

    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)

        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)

        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

        normal_dev = False,

            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.

    if normal_dev:

    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.

packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/tools/: - An element keeps its `[ref=eN]` across `.ax()`/`find()` reads until its role or label changes; a ref whose element is missing from the window's last two `.ax()` snapshots throws `StaleRef`. Re-snapshot; NEVER guess. On macOS, an element action also refuses with `StaleRef`, sending nothing, if its element now reads with another role or label; the error gives that element a new ref (`eN now reads as textfield "Street" [ref=eM]`). A destroyed-element refusal may name the one candidate with the original role, labels and value, only after whole-window reads. A relabelled-element refusal may instead name the one other candidate this read of the window found with the original role and label, even if the read was cut short by `maxDepth` or a node limit; unseen matches may exist. Equal fields do not prove a candidate is the same control: check it before acting on it.

# An identifier that represent common dependencies (unconditional).
_COMMON_CONDITION = ""

def _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps):
    """Flatten a list of dependency maps into one dictionary.

    Dependency maps have the following structure:

    ```python
    DEPENDENCIES_MAP = {
        # The first key in the map is a Bazel package
        # name of the workspace this file is defined in.
        "workspace_member_package": {

            # Not all dependencies are supported for all platforms.
            # the condition key is the condition required to be true
            # on the host platform.
            "condition": {

                # An alias to a crate target.     # The label of the crate target the
                # Aliases are only crate names.   # package name refers to.
                "package_name":                   "@full//:label",
            }
        }
    }
    ```

    Args:
        all_dependency_maps (list): A list of dicts as described above

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary as described above
    """
    dependencies = {}

    for workspace_deps_map in all_dependency_maps:
        for pkg_name, conditional_deps_map in workspace_deps_map.items():
            if pkg_name not in dependencies:
                non_frozen_map = dict()
                for key, values in conditional_deps_map.items():
                    non_frozen_map.update({key: dict(values.items())})
                dependencies.setdefault(pkg_name, non_frozen_map)
                continue

            for condition, deps_map in conditional_deps_map.items():
                # If the condition has not been recorded, do so and continue
                if condition not in dependencies[pkg_name]:
                    dependencies[pkg_name].setdefault(condition, dict(deps_map.items()))
                    continue

                # Alert on any miss-matched dependencies
                inconsistent_entries = []
                for crate_name, crate_label in deps_map.items():
                    existing = dependencies[pkg_name][condition].get(crate_name)
                    if existing and existing != crate_label:
                        inconsistent_entries.append((crate_name, existing, crate_label))
                    dependencies[pkg_name][condition].update({crate_name: crate_label})

    return dependencies

def crate_deps(deps, package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of the requested crates for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        deps (list): The desired list of crate targets.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()`.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if not deps:
        return []

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Join both sets of dependencies
    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps([
        _NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES,
        _NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
        _PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_DEPENDENCIES,
        _BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES,
    ]).pop(package_name, {})

    # Combine all conditional packages so we can easily index over a flat list
    # TODO: Perhaps this should actually return select statements and maintain
    # the conditionals of the dependencies
    flat_deps = {}
    for deps_set in dependencies.values():
        for crate_name, crate_label in deps_set.items():
            flat_deps.update({crate_name: crate_label})

    missing_crates = []
    crate_targets = []
    for crate_target in deps:
        if crate_target not in flat_deps:
            missing_crates.append(crate_target)
        else:
            crate_targets.append(flat_deps[crate_target])

    if missing_crates:
        fail("Could not find crates `{}` among dependencies of `{}`. Available dependencies were `{}`".format(
            missing_crates,
            package_name,
            dependencies,
        ))

    return crate_targets

def crate_edition(package_name = None):
    """Finds the Rust edition for the package where this macro is called.

    Args:
        package_name (str, optional): The package name whose edition should be
            looked up. Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        str: The Rust edition declared by the package's Cargo.toml file.
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    if package_name not in _CRATE_EDITIONS:
        fail("Tried to get crate_edition for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")

    return _CRATE_EDITIONS[package_name]

def all_crate_deps(
        normal = False, 
        normal_dev = False, 
        proc_macro = False, 
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Finds the fully qualified label of all requested direct crate dependencies \
    for the package where this macro is called.

    If no parameters are set, all normal dependencies are returned. Setting any one flag will
    otherwise impact the contents of the returned list.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list.
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        list: A list of labels to generated rust targets (str)
    """

    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_dependency_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_DEPENDENCIES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_DEPENDENCIES)

    # Default to always using normal dependencies
    if not all_dependency_maps:
        all_dependency_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEPENDENCIES)

    dependencies = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_dependency_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not dependencies:
        if dependencies == None:
            fail("Tried to get all_crate_deps for package " + package_name + " but that package had no Cargo.toml file")
        else:
            return []

    crate_deps = list(dependencies.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).values())
    for condition, deps in dependencies.items():
        crate_deps += selects.with_or({
            tuple(_CONDITIONS[condition]): deps.values(),
            "//conditions:default": [],
        })

    return crate_deps

def aliases(
        normal = False,
        normal_dev = False,
        proc_macro = False,
        proc_macro_dev = False,
        build = False,
        build_proc_macro = False,
        package_name = None):
    """Produces a map of Crate alias names to their original label

    If no dependency kinds are specified, `normal` and `proc_macro` are used by default.
    Setting any one flag will otherwise determine the contents of the returned dict.

    Args:
        normal (bool, optional): If True, normal dependencies are included in the
            output list.
        normal_dev (bool, optional): If True, normal dev dependencies will be
            included in the output list..
        proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, proc_macro dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        proc_macro_dev (bool, optional): If True, dev proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        build (bool, optional): If True, build dependencies are included
            in the output list.
        build_proc_macro (bool, optional): If True, build proc_macro dependencies are
            included in the output list.
        package_name (str, optional): The package name of the set of dependencies to look up.
            Defaults to `native.package_name()` when unset.

    Returns:
        dict: The aliases of all associated packages
    """
    if package_name == None:
        package_name = native.package_name()

    # Determine the relevant maps to use
    all_aliases_maps = []
    if normal:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
    if normal_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_DEV_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)
    if proc_macro_dev:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_DEV_ALIASES)
    if build:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_ALIASES)
    if build_proc_macro:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_BUILD_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    # Default to always using normal aliases
    if not all_aliases_maps:
        all_aliases_maps.append(_NORMAL_ALIASES)
        all_aliases_maps.append(_PROC_MACRO_ALIASES)

    aliases = _flatten_dependency_maps(all_aliases_maps).pop(package_name, None)

    if not aliases:
        return dict()

    common_items = aliases.pop(_COMMON_CONDITION, {}).items()

    # If there are only common items in the dictionary, immediately return them
    if not len(aliases.keys()) == 1:
        return dict(common_items)

    # Build a single select statement where each conditional has accounted for the
    # common set of aliases.
    crate_aliases = {"//conditions:default": dict(common_items)}
    for condition, deps in aliases.items():
        condition_triples = _CONDITIONS[condition]
        for triple in condition_triples:
            if triple in crate_aliases:
                crate_aliases[triple].update(deps)
            else:
                crate_aliases.update({triple: dict(deps.items() + common_items)})

    return select(crate_aliases)

packages/browser-relay/README.md: - Chrome refuses the debugger in a tab while another extension's frame, such as a password manager's inline menu, is in it. In a tab omp drives, the extension empties and hides that frame so omp can continue; your other tabs keep theirs. The call that ran into the frame, or a later one on that tab, names the extension and the frame's page, so the agent can tell you what was hidden; nothing is saved through a hidden frame.
packages/coding-agent/src/tools/browser/: // The title is the other extension's own text, so it is labelled as such rather than as a name Chrome vouches for.

return `Nothing was saved: omp emptied and hid ${named.join(", and ")} in this tab, for the user as well, because Chrome lets omp do nothing in a tab while another extension's frame is open in it. If that frame offered to save a login, the login was not saved and the prompt is gone; never tell the user a login was saved or that the prompt is still there. In your final reply, tell the user that nothing was saved and what omp hid.`;
// Puppeteer's protocol map cannot express the relay-private method; the send signature is otherwise identical.
const session = page.mainFrame().client as unknown as { send(method: string): Promise<unknown> };
// A relay of an older omp forwards the unknown method to Chrome, which rejects it.

docs/tools/computer.md: On macOS, `setValue(text)` on a native text field, text area or combo box replaces its whole value the way `win.type` inserts text, so the app handles the edit as typed input: a search field searches, and a field with suggestions may offer them. An unfocused field is focused first only when its app is not the frontmost one, where focusing it would move the user's caret; such a field, a secure text field, and an element without a settable selection are written through `AXValue` instead, which some apps show without storing. A background field focused for the write keeps its app's focus afterwards, since some apps drop an edit whose field loses focus before it is committed. Either way the field is read back, and a value other than `text` throws `AxFailed` giving how many characters were written and what the field reads now. The written text is never quoted, and neither is what a secure field reads; a field that reads back as mask characters is described as masked. A field that reads back as a mask exactly as long as `text` (a password field, whatever role it reports) counts as a successful write; a mask of another length still fails. Web content, terminals and the fields of Chromium-based apps (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Electron apps; use `el.type(text)` there) are refused before anything is written.

docs/computer-use.md: macOS background pointer input also covers drags, mouse holds, clicks with modifiers, right-clicks, and scrolls in Electron apps, all without moving the user's pointer. During a background drag a web page reports `buttons` as 0, because the real button is up. A drag that picks up an item for drag and drop (a file, a table row, a font tile, selected text) starts a session that macOS completes from the user's real pointer as well as from the drag: on macOS 26.5 a Finder file followed the user's moving pointer into their own Finder window or onto the Desktop. Which elements start such a session is up to each application, so a background left-button drag or mouse hold runs only when it starts on a slider, scroll bar, splitter, value indicator or stepper, as the element at its start point reports through accessibility. A plain left drag whose first and last points lie on the text of one native text view, such as a TextEdit document, is made as that view's selection through accessibility instead, with no mouse event, and `drag` returns the selection read back; a press on selected text, a link or an attachment, which would pick it up, does not count, nor does right-to-left text, where the caret's side of a character depends on its run. Web page text has no such route: Chrome lets an assistive client select only editable web text, and places a point in page text only in its screen-reader mode. Anywhere else the drag or hold has no background route, so `computer.backgroundFallback` applies before anything is sent. As a backstop, a session that begins anyway sends the drag back to where it started, releases it there and throws `InputFailed`; read the target before retrying, and prefer the app's menu command or AX. It is not rerun in takeover, which could repeat a drop that landed. Drags inside a view (sliders, text selections, a web page's mouse-driven drag) are unaffected. A drag that starts on a control publishing its value (a slider, scroll bar or splitter) reads that value before and after: when it has not changed, and the path neither ended where it started nor pushed the control against the end it already sat at (for a splitter or stepper, either end), the call throws `InputFailed` saying no change was observed; read the target before retrying. A web page may take the press of a background drag and none of its moves, so when a plain left drag leaves a slider in web content where it was, or at the value under the press, the slider is stepped on with `AXIncrement` or `AXDecrement` to the value under the path's end: the first step is confirmed and gives the step size, the rest go out together, and the value is read until it settles. A slider the pointer moved is not stepped, nor one whose value is far from the one under the point pressed (a slider laid out right to left), which throws `InputFailed` instead. One drag takes at most 1000 steps; one that needs more, or whose slider settles short of where its steps lead, throws `InputFailed` naming the value it reached, and a slider that takes neither the pointer nor a step throws `InputFailed` saying no change was observed. An open menu takes the keyboard from the user's application, so a right-click or Control-click, or a click, `press()` or `perform("AXShowMenu")` on a menu button or popup button, that opens one in a background application closes it before the call returns; the call then throws `InputFailed`, because the input was delivered, and lists the menu's items: inspect the target before retrying. It is never rerun in takeover, because handing focus back closes the menu again; pass `menu` instead, as below. Before a press on a menu button or popup button, its window is made key within its application, as for a background left click, so the items read enabled as they would in an active application. A mouse hold or drag with the right button or Control, or a right-click or Control-click with `count` above 1, has no background route, since its menu would stay open until the button is released or the later clicks are sent, so `computer.backgroundFallback` applies before anything is sent. So does a left-button hold, drag, or click with `count` above 1 on a menu button or popup button, whose menu opens on the first press: click the control once with `menu` instead. Drags and holds with `keys` go only once the application reports keyboard focus in the target, and refuse as keystrokes do when another window, such as a sheet attached to it, has the focus or takes it during the gesture; a drag or hold into a sheet or popover holding the focus gets only the activation, as a click into it does, so it stays open; gestures with modifiers or `keys` into Apple Screen Sharing have no background route either, as held keys there do not. Presses into an app built on Tk 8.6 or later have no background route, because that Tk places them at the user's real pointer, so `computer.backgroundFallback` applies; macOS's own Tk 8.5 takes them in the background.

rows.label: ax-read-as-title-link
rows.title: fix(natives): keep a macOS ref whose own label changes while its title element shows the same text
reasons: held: Will, 2026-11-13: Main decides the approach once #19061 merges, with all the data in. Data so far: release leg 9 refusals in 93 runs (4 true catches, 5 same-control relabels, about +2 steps each, no grade changed); wording-only change closed (no step saved, 6 runs per arm); TitleTwin 0 wrong-item actions in 200 trials on stock apps, fixture same-title reuse 10/10 wrong; RelabelCases (scripted, 10 tries per case, v18.20.0 vs b42c6d20412, ~/tmp/oh-my-pi/RelabelCases/{signals,recovery}.md): Reminders count refused 10/10 -> right control 10/10; Finder rename and Calendar location still refused 10/10 (no title link); Contacts City->Street still refused 10/10. Finder and Calendar differ from Contacts in that frame, value and sibling count are unchanged, but that is not shown safe in general. A refusal that carried its parent's subtree would be an estimated 150-460 chars against the 1,300-7,400 the model re-read, and would save one of the two recovery steps (reconstructed, not run).
